source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 5 May 1949, p. 3 ("Election nominations": Lisburn); Lisburn Standard, 6 May 1949, p. 4 ("No Lisburn election"); Lisburn Standard, 10 June 1949, p. 4 ("Lisburn Urban Council")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: Image-read (page crops of p. 3, col. 4 foot and col. 5 head): "There will be no contests in Lisburn Urban District"; nominations listed by ward with seat counts. INA copy: https://irishnewsarchive.com/?a=d&d=BNL19490505.1.3; South Ward (four seats), only three names (Munn, Greer, Dick). Lisburn Standard 6 May 1949 p. 4 (image-read, page crop): all three wards returned unopposed, "but in the South Ward no nomination papers were received from Mr. Jas. M'Keown"; it is "probable" that he will be deemed to be re-elected unless he declines. Lisburn Standard 10 June 1949 p. 4 (image-read, page crop, gaps-rest): at the council's monthly meeting, the first after the May returns, the members present include James M'Keown, so the fourth South seat went to him.

note: Triennial whole-council election of Lisburn Urban District Council (calendar polling day 18 May 1949); no poll: nominations on 4 May 1949 were 6 for Central, 5 for North and 3 for the 4 South Ward seats, all returned unopposed (Belfast News-Letter, 5 May 1949, p. 3); the retiring member Jas. M'Keown, who was not nominated, was deemed re-elected to the fourth South seat (Lisburn Standard, 6 May 1949, p. 4), and sat as a member at the council's June meeting (Lisburn Standard, 10 June 1949, p. 4). Three nominated for four seats; the fourth seat went to the retiring member Jas. M'Keown, who was not nominated, under reg. 15(2) (insufficient nominations): he was deemed re-elected and sat at the council's June 1949 meeting. James A. M'Keown was the fourth South Ward member elected in 1946 and again in 1952.
